note: New version line; unrelated to historical v1 builds.
appearanceOrder: Random per team; Sets 1-6 use each team member once.
setFormat: 1v1, first to 2 race wins. Valid set scores: 2-0 or 2-1.
ace: If team score is 3-3 after Set 6, Set 7 ace decider. Repeat appearance allowed; ace is randomly selected in v1.0.0.
flow: Play entire current set automatically until one player reaches 2 race wins
ui: Live league-side rendering throttled to ~12.5Hz while physics remains 50Hz.
heatEnd: First player to clear wins the heat immediately.
mapOrder: All 9 maps are shuffled. Each heat uses the next map. After all 9 are used, the deck reshuffles.
bracketMapDisplay: Sets 1-6 show a preassigned random map next to the player matchup.
aceDisplay: Set 7 is always visible as ??? vs ???. If Sets 1-6 finish 3-3, ??? is replaced by randomly selected ace player names.
mapAssignment: One random map per set; all races inside that set use the same assigned map.
bracketLayout: Map name is green. Blue/A player is right-aligned immediately left of VS; Red/B player is immediately right of VS.
teamColors: A team = BLUE, B team = RED; race unit/fallback colors follow team color.
bracketAlignment: Matchup block shifted slightly left for better visual centering.
liveSideLayout: B/red player names in 1S-6S rows are aligned to the far right.
avoidanceAI: Front-threat detection, emergency reaction, and Destiny Gate threat reads were strengthened to reduce obvious straight-line deaths after observer-count reduction.
spaceMapAI: Space map no longer center-locks racers; it uses wider lane bias and faster threat scanning.
teamColor: A/BLUE and B/RED are unified across unit body and nickname plate.
sparseObserverAI: With only 1-3 nearby observers, racers use stronger proactive forward prediction and wider safe dodges.
bracket: A/B banned maps are displayed above Set 1.
drivingVariety: Each player has a persistent lane/risk personality plus rare controlled variant lines, so two racers no longer mirror each other.
survivalTarget: Targeting roughly 3-5x higher practical survival than v1.0.9.
closeThreat: Nearby/forward observers are detected every tick with deterministic emergency avoidance.
priority: Survival score absolutely dominates route length and speed.
runtimeFix: Fixed Survival Master runtime crash caused by Python-style boolean identifier `True` inside JavaScript planner code.
hardDodgeSafety: Emergency lane values are clamped to a finite ±3.6 range.
survivalAI: Continuous forward safety-field lane evaluation added; obvious nearby threats are detected earlier and wide dodge is held longer.
controlVariety: Safe-road human-like control frequency raised slightly; feint/cutback/doublemove receive a little more weight.
pathVariety: Per-player lane and dodge personality reduces mirrored paths between the two racers.
rootFix: Survival/variant lane choices are now applied to actual movement; the old NORMAL center-spline motion no longer overwrites them.
closeReaction: Hard-close threats bypass reaction delay and trigger immediate avoidance.
motionStability: Simulation dt capped at 34ms, forward movement capped per tick, lateral steering acceleration-limited.
teleportFix: Visual interpolation catch-up distance is bounded to prevent apparent teleporting after frame hitches.
evadeStability: Active emergency dodge will not instantly reverse direction on the next threat scan.
performance: Keeps v1.9.7 pruned two-pass corridor search and 3x/5x adaptive substeps.
emergency: Emergency entry is slightly earlier (0.13-0.20s by density), hard-check horizon raised to 0.28s, and action duration raised to 150ms.
cornerStability: Spline tangent is blended around corners; logical segment changes are limited to one step per tick; lateral steering is damped by turn angle.
speedStability: Simulation dt capped at 24ms; per-frame catch-up is limited to two fixed steps to prevent apparent multi-speed bursts.
laneStability: Safety lane cannot instantly reverse through a sharp corner.
movementEngine: UnifiedMovement120: only one engine writes racer x/y during gameplay.
stats: Player stats still affect route quality, clearance, steering precision and consistency rather than whether obvious danger is noticed.
legacy: Legacy teleport guards, old rejoin projection, old segment road correction and old coordinate recovery are bypassed by the new updatePlayer.
frameStability: At most 2 simulation catch-up steps per render frame; excess backlog is discarded rather than fast-forwarded.
motionFix: Center position, heading normal and road width are continuously filtered through corners, preventing lane-offset coordinate jumps.
cameraFix: Legacy close-battle/overtake/pack camera offsets are removed from live racing; camera uses unified path frame and 900ms leader hysteresis.
frameFix: At most one simulation movement step is executed per rendered frame; extra backlog is dropped instead of appearing as a burst.
cornerMotion: Racers now integrate forward position incrementally and turn heading continuously; path correction is soft/capped, so they no longer stop then snap direction.
teleportGuard: Single-tick physical movement capped at 0.32; old fixed-step backlog is zeroed instead of retained near a full step.
neonDrift: 9-to-11 vertical inside section restricts the problematic outer/right lane and biases racers inward.
pathing: Spline is reference-only; racers choose short local trajectories across the full road width.
avoidance: Unsafe paths are rejected based on reachable trajectory; a small emergency slowdown is allowed only when all reachable paths are poor.
controls: Low-probability zigzag, wide-line, hold-line, feint and cutback remain; danger cancels them immediately.
emergencyAvoidance: Near-contact situations trigger a dense 10-lane side-escape search before normal planning.
stoppedObservers: Stopped observers are treated as static walls with larger safety margins instead of being projected away.
humanControls: zigzag/wide/hold/feint/cutback/doublemove occur at a low but more visible frequency; danger cancels them.
competitionAI: Close racers actively avoid mirroring each other's lane choice; when overlapped they bias toward opposite routes.
chaseMode: A significantly trailing racer prioritizes the calculated inside/fast line with a modest speed boost until the gap closes; immediate observer danger still overrides.
stopControl: Frequency reduced by 95%; remaining activations are shorter and less severe.
simpleThreat: 1-2 observer situations trigger earlier and use a larger safety radius.
escapeHold: After a simple-threat dodge, the racer holds the safe side briefly instead of immediately returning to the old route.
stoppedObserver: Stopped observers receive extra clearance margin.
target: Approximately 99% survival goal; not guaranteed in physically blocked states.
planner: Three-stage trajectory beam search with ~2s+ future prediction.
behavior: Wide escapes remain available only as emergency candidates; small human-like dodges receive a strong preference.
startFix: League Set 1 can now start without the Survival Master planner throwing a ReferenceError.
stopFix: Actual zero-speed stop-control is now possible; old minimum 65% speed clamp removed.
naturalFlow: Long full stops removed. Dense danger now uses slow rolling avoidance and short hesitation.
crowdWait: ~70-125ms hesitation only, moving at low speed instead of full stop.
replan: Crowd danger plans refresh faster (~110ms) so racers resume acceleration as soon as a gap opens.
slowControl: Heavy slowdown behavior reduced by approximately 95%; lateral avoidance now carries most evasive behavior.
collisionVeto: Every tick, the final intended route is tested against nearby observers over ~0.1-0.9s. Unsafe plans are immediately cancelled.
planAuthority: Crowd/free/control plans lose authority instantly when the veto layer predicts a collision.
steering: Threat-burst lateral authority is 4.60x; speed remains high and slowdown is not the primary defense.
survival: Execution AI has its own protected state and runs its A->B->C sequence until completion or material threat change.
chainEvade: Sequential threats are re-evaluated immediately; prior escape direction is only softly biased, not hard-locked.
veto: Lookahead increased to ~1.42s with 16 lane candidates; hold reduced to ~240ms.
naturalMotion: Emergency target lateral speed is stronger but steering acceleration is softened for curved, human-looking dodges.
crowdBreakout: 3+ simultaneous nearby observers trigger a dedicated open-space density search before normal collision veto.
reaction: Near-instant danger detection and steering response; naturalness is secondary to survival.
holds: Veto and breakout directional holds reduced to ~100ms / ~90ms.
singleObserver: Exactly one nearby threatening observer gets absolute-priority hard escape every tick.
competition: Anti-mirror logic strengthened so close 1v1 racers choose visibly different lanes more often.
motion: Global lateral range reduced further; local small evasions are preferred before any full-width maneuver.

cleanup.method: Removed only named legacy functions whose identifier appeared exactly once (definition only).

safeCorridor: 11 lane corridors x 4 speed choices, about 0.95s lookahead.
threatBurst: Racers stay calm when the road is clear, but enter a hyper-reactive lateral dodge mode whenever observers threaten the corridor.
multiThreat: 2+ simultaneous threats can trigger alternating zig-zag breakout moves at ~85-120ms cadence.
prediction: Reachable-trajectory prediction now uses the exact same lateral dynamics as real movement.
zigzag: Threat-burst zigzag now requires 3+ threats, switches more slowly, and uses lower amplitude.
racingLine: Optimal-line influence reduced heavily on clear roads and almost removed from free-driving blend.
slowdown: When all reachable paths are poor, a short 10-25% slowdown is allowed to create real avoidance time.
architecture: Only one survival planner may overwrite the calm-road driving decision. Older danger layers remain defined for compatibility but are bypassed by updatePlayer.
collisionModel: Planner risk uses the player's physical hit radius plus a small safety margin to better match real collision behavior.
speed: Visible player/observer movement speed remains 1x; the same 20ms of game time is simply simulated in five smaller pieces.
physics: Lateral velocity is now stored in lane-units/second and integrated once with dt; 20ms x1 and 4ms x5 produce equivalent real-time motion.
rootCause: v1.8.0 scaled lateral acceleration and lateral displacement by substep time, effectively weakening evasive movement during 5x substeps.
testMode: Survival Gauntlet button starts deterministic forced-threat waves instead of relying on lucky observer spacing.
debug: HUD records attempts, clears, deaths, waves passed, and last-death action/predicted minimum gap/actual gap/lane/progress.
goal: Raise single-front and multi-threat pass rates by improving actual collision escape execution.
analytics: Adds Execution failure count plus Emergency entry delay and Execution repeated-threat death categories.
predictionFix: Observer future velocity is clamped to plausible physical speed.
sensorFix: Danger substeps rebuild the spatial grid every microstep; unified survival uses direct scan fallback.
reactionMetric: Threat first seen -> first evasive command.
telemetry: Tracks special-control attempts, completions and interruptions separately.
emergencyEscape: Imminent collision bypasses normal racing logic and selects the quickest physically reachable side exit.
continuousReplan: Emergency escape is recalculated every update; previous escape direction is never hard-locked.
speedPolicy: Direct-ahead threats may use mild braking; offset threats can keep or slightly raise forward speed.
earlyEscape: Pre-emptive avoidance begins at roughly 2.4-7.2 units.
escapeReserve: Corridor scoring now rewards future lateral escape room and penalizes edge trapping.
twoStagePrediction: Immediate safety evaluated to ~0.78s and continuation safety to ~1.32s.
specialControls: Special controls have a protected state and are interrupted only by actual predicted collision.
safety: Any survival planner activation immediately cancels special controls.
corridor: Center-first Safe Corridor: normal candidates stay within ~76% of road width. Edge corridors unlock only when center candidates remain unsafe.
edgeControl: Edge penalty strengthened; continuity bias prevents unnecessary full-width hopping.
survivalExecution: Safe Corridor keeps short execution authority while still hard-hit free; Emergency fallback tightened to TTC <= 0.10s unless corridor predicts a hard hit.
chainedSurvival: Corridor selection evaluates immediate, mid and far safety plus whether a usable left/right escape remains after the first dodge.
executionAI: Fresh corridor plans are converted into short A->B->C movement sequences. The executor owns movement briefly and replans only on material threat changes.
verifiedSurvival: Chained survival success is credited only after surviving ~1.3 seconds in real simulation, not because a future option merely existed.
auditFixes: Centralized action ownership into a single state machine.
Removed concurrent per-tick competition between special, survival and emergency logic.
Prevented emergency fallback from being counted multiple times per microstep.
Added reset for state-machine and emergency-action stale state.

stateMachine.rule: Exactly one state owns movement at a time.

executionCompletion: A/B/C stages now complete on actual lane arrival or per-stage timeout, instead of relying on a single global expiry.
partialReplan: Material threat changes modify only remaining B/C stages where possible; full plan reset is reserved for sudden near threats.
executionFinishFix: Execution now explicitly releases SURVIVAL state after finish/failure, clears stale plan ownership, and applies a 55ms post-finish cooldown before creating a new corridor plan.
